strategy.summary: The todo app (public/app.js, in-memory state per page) lets users tick todos complete, filter All/Active/Completed with aria-pressed on the selected filter button, and clear completed todos with a button that is hidden unless a todo is completed. Playwright e2e tests against the real static server must prove each criterion through what the user sees: strike-through, the items-left count, the listed titles, pressed state and the Clear completed button.
inScope: Completing and un-completing todos via the checkbox (strike-through and items-left count)
All / Active / Completed filters and their pressed state
outOfScope: Adding todos (covered by tests/add-todo.spec.js) beyond using it as setup
Persistence across reloads (app keeps todos in memory only; ticket doesn't ask)
Editing or deleting single todos (not in ticket)
assumptions: The real app runs for real: Playwright's existing webServer starts node server.js on 4173; nothing is faked (no backend API exists; state lives in the page).
Each test opens a fresh page, so todos are isolated per test without cleanup.
'Struck through' is checked as the computed text-decoration-line: line-through of the todo's title span (styles.css li.completed span), and its absence when not completed.
'Shown as pressed' means aria-pressed="true" on the selected filter button and "false" on the others, as app.js sets it.

risks.description: Count or filter logic regression leaves wrong todos visible or wrong count
risks.mitigation: Assert exact title arrays (in order) and exact count text in every case

risks.description: Clear completed removes active todos or only one completed todo
risks.mitigation: TC7 clears two completed todos among an active one and asserts the remaining list exactly

risks.description: Re-render under a filter detaches the checkbox, causing flaky check() calls
risks.mitigation: Use click() on the checkbox where the row leaves the view and assert the resulting list

acceptanceCriteria.text: Ticking a todo's checkbox marks it completed: it is struck through and the items-left count goes down by one; unticking reverses both.
Active shows only not-completed todos, Completed only completed ones, All every todo; the selected filter is shown as pressed.
"Clear completed" is shown only while at least one todo is completed, and removes every completed todo.

testCases.title: ticking a todo strikes it through and lowers the items-left count by one
preconditions: Fresh page with todos 'Buy milk' and 'Walk dog'
steps: Check that 'Buy milk' is not struck through and count reads '2 items left'
testCases.expected: Checkbox checked, 'Buy milk' title has line-through, 'Walk dog' doesn't, count reads '1 item left'

testCases.title: unticking a completed todo removes the strike-through and raises the count again
preconditions: Fresh page with 'Buy milk' and 'Walk dog', 'Buy milk' ticked (1 item left)
testCases.expected: Checkbox unchecked, no line-through, count reads '2 items left'

testCases.title: Active filter shows only todos that aren't completed and is shown as pressed
preconditions: Todos 'Buy milk', 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent'; 'Walk dog' ticked
testCases.expected: List shows exactly ['Buy milk','Pay rent']; Active aria-pressed=true, All and Completed false

testCases.title: Completed filter shows only completed todos and is shown as pressed
preconditions: Todos 'Buy milk', 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent'; 'Walk dog' ticked
testCases.expected: List shows exactly ['Walk dog']; Completed aria-pressed=true, All and Active false

testCases.title: All filter shows every todo in order and is shown as pressed
preconditions: Todos 'Buy milk', 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent'; 'Walk dog' ticked; Completed filter selected
testCases.expected: List shows exactly ['Buy milk','Walk dog','Pay rent'] in order; All aria-pressed=true, others false
testCases.rationale: Returning to All restores every todo

testCases.title: ticking a todo under the Active filter removes it from the view
preconditions: Todos 'Buy milk', 'Walk dog'; Active filter selected
testCases.expected: List shows exactly ['Walk dog']; count '1 item left'
testCases.rationale: Filter applies to state changes made while it is selected

testCases.title: Clear completed is hidden until a todo is completed and hidden again once it is unticked
steps: Assert list loaded and Clear completed hidden
Tick 'Buy milk' and assert button visible
testCases.expected: Button hidden, then visible, then hidden again
testCases.rationale: Button is unavailable when there is nothing to clear

testCases.title: Clear completed removes every completed todo and keeps the active ones
preconditions: Todos 'Buy milk', 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent'; 'Buy milk' and 'Pay rent' ticked
testCases.expected: List shows exactly ['Walk dog'], count '1 item left', Clear completed hidden
testCases.rationale: Removes all completed, not just one, and no active ones

strategy.environmentNotes: Playwright webServer in playwright.config.js starts `node server.js` on http://localhost:4173 (BASE_URL in runs). No backend, no seed data.

review.standard: Playwright rules: never use XPath, CSS selectors (classes, chains); General: avoid brittle selectors that rely on DOM structure
review.summary: `titles` finds each todo's title with the CSS tag selector `locator('span')` inside each listitem, so the list assertions depend on the app's inner markup, not on what the user sees.
review.failureScenario: In app.js the title is a `<span>` inside a `<label>`. Suppose a refactor renders the title as a plain text node in the label, or wraps it in `<strong>`, and the app still works. Then `titles(page)` matches nothing (or extra elements), and every `toHaveText([...])` list assertion fails: the one in addTodos and those in TC3, TC4, TC5, TC6 and TC8. A listitem's text is already just the title, because the checkbox adds no text. So `todoList(page).getByRole('listitem')` with `toHaveText(names)`, as tests/add-todo.spec.js does, checks the same exact titles in order without the tag selector.
